value.body: A behaviour therapist works one-on-one with children who have autism or other developmental conditions, teaching communication, daily living and social skills through structured, play-based sessions. Employers include child development centres, therapy clinics, special schools and home-based therapy services. A typical day involves several sessions, careful data recording and short updates to parents.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BA or B.Sc in Psychology plus training in Applied Behaviour Analysis (ABA)

items.label: Works under
items.value: A supervising psychologist or certified behaviour analyst

items.label: Common setting
items.value: Therapy centres, special schools, home visits

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join a therapy centre as a trainee and complete an in-house or external ABA training while working under supervision. Some take an international behaviour-technician certificate. Patience with children and comfort working with families matter as much as theory.

value.title: At a glance
items: This is not the same as a clinical psychologist role; licensed practice needs further study and RCI registration.
Work is often emotionally demanding but direct and hands-on.
Next roles: senior therapist, programme supervisor, or further study in clinical or rehabilitation psychology.
